note: Seed text written for the demo; not yet reviewed by SWS (OT-04). Keyed for now by WHM issue type; map to Siteimprove rule or policy IDs once known. Types for live Siteimprove rules (Nov 20) map through siteimproveIds such as "a11y-rule:113". Stanford policies map through "policy:<id>" (allowlisted policies only, decisions Nov 20).

types.title: Images are missing text descriptions
types.what: Some images have no alternative text, so people using screen readers don’t know what the image shows.
types.why: Text descriptions are required at WCAG level A. Missing ones are among the most common barriers for blind visitors.
types.todo: Edit each image listed below and add a short description of what it shows. Decorative images can be marked as decorative instead.

types.title: Link text doesn’t say where the link goes
types.what: Links use wording like “click here” or “read more” that only makes sense with the text around it.
types.why: People who move through a page by its links hear the link text on its own.
types.todo: Rewrite each link so its words name the destination, for example “Read the accessibility guide.”

types.title: Links lead to pages that don’t exist
types.what: These links point to pages that return a “not found” error.
types.why: Broken links send visitors to a dead end and make the site look out of date.
types.todo: Update each link to the right address, or remove it if the page is gone for good.

types.title: PDFs may not work with screen readers
types.what: These PDFs aren’t tagged, so their structure can’t be read by assistive technology.
types.why: Untagged PDFs can be unreadable for screen reader users.
types.todo: Replace the PDF with a web page where possible, or re-export it as a tagged PDF.

types.title: Some text is too light to read easily
types.what: A few text styles don’t have enough contrast against their background.
types.why: Low contrast makes text hard to read for many visitors, especially on phones outdoors.
types.todo: No action needed from you. This comes from the site template, and SWS is handling it.

types.title: Pages not updated in over a year
types.what: These pages haven’t changed in more than 12 months. (In this demo the age check is simulated; the data source is still being chosen.)
types.why: Out-of-date content is the most common reason site owners make changes. Some pages are fine as they are, such as a page updated once a year.
types.todo: Check each page. Update it, or choose “They’re still correct” if it doesn’t need a change.

types.title: Pages share the same title
types.what: Several pages use the same page title.
types.why: In search results, visitors can’t tell these pages apart.
types.todo: Give each page a title that describes what is on it.

types.title: Pages are missing a search description
types.what: These pages have no summary for search engines to show.
types.why: Without one, search engines pick text from the page, which may not help visitors decide to click.
types.todo: Add a one- or two-sentence summary in each page’s search description field.

types.title: Uses an outdated office name
types.what: These pages use a name that Stanford has replaced.
types.why: A Stanford content policy checks for retired names so messages stay consistent across sites.
types.todo: Replace the old name with the current one on each page.

types.title: Some buttons or links are too small to tap easily
types.what: Some buttons or links are smaller than 24 by 24 pixels and sit close to other controls.
types.why: Small, crowded controls are hard to tap for people with limited hand movement and for anyone on a phone. WCAG level AA asks for this size or enough space around it.
types.todo: Make each listed button or link bigger, or add space around it.

types.title: Some headings have nothing under them
types.what: Some headings are followed right away by another heading or by the end of the page.
types.why: People who skim by headings expect each one to introduce something. Empty headings are confusing, especially with a screen reader.
types.todo: Add content under each listed heading, or remove the heading if it isn’t needed.

types.title: Pages don’t start with a main heading
types.what: These pages don’t begin with a level 1 heading.
types.why: The main heading tells visitors and screen readers what the page is about before they read further.
types.todo: Make sure each listed page starts with one level 1 heading that names the page.

types.title: Headings skip levels
types.what: Some pages jump from one heading level to a lower one, such as from Heading 2 to Heading 4.
types.why: Screen reader users rely on heading levels to understand how a page is organized. Skipped levels make that harder.
types.todo: Change the headings so each level follows the one above it without skipping.

types.title: Buttons and links are smaller than the recommended size
types.what: Buttons and links are smaller than 44 by 44 pixels, the size recommended at WCAG level AAA.
types.why: Larger controls are easier for everyone to tap, especially on phones.
types.todo: No action needed from you. This comes from the site template, and SWS is handling it.

types.title: Lines of text are close together
types.what: The space between lines in paragraphs is less than 1.5 times the text size, the level recommended at WCAG level AAA.
types.why: More space between lines makes long text easier to read, especially for people with dyslexia or low vision.
types.todo: No action needed from you. This comes from the site template, and SWS is handling it.

types.title: Some text doesn’t meet the higher contrast level
types.what: Some text has enough contrast for WCAG level AA but not for the stricter level AAA.
types.why: Higher contrast helps people with low vision read more easily.
types.todo: No action needed from you. This comes from the site template, and SWS is handling it.

types.title: Links in the shared header or footer are reported broken
types.what: Siteimprove reports some links in the shared Stanford header or footer as broken on every page.
types.why: These links come from the site template, not from your content. They may be false alarms caused by how the check visits those sites.
types.todo: No action needed from you. SWS is looking into it.

types.title: Links to Stanford sites use http instead of https
types.what: Some links to stanford.edu addresses start with http:// instead of https://.
types.why: Stanford sites use secure (https) addresses. An insecure link adds a redirect and can trigger a browser warning.
types.todo: Change each link so it starts with https://.

types.title: Links show a web address instead of words
types.what: Some links use the web address itself as the link text, such as “www.stanford.edu.”
types.why: Screen readers read an address out character by character, and an address doesn’t tell visitors where the link goes.
types.todo: Replace each address with words that name the destination, such as “Stanford home page.”

types.title: Words typed in all capital letters
types.what: Some text is typed in all capital letters.
types.why: All-caps text is harder to read, especially for people with dyslexia, and it can read as shouting.
types.todo: Retype the text with normal capitals. To make it stand out, use a heading or bold text instead.

types.title: Paragraphs are very long
types.what: Some paragraphs are longer than 600 characters, about 100 words.
types.why: Short paragraphs are easier to read and skim, especially on a phone.
types.todo: Break each long paragraph into shorter ones of about 40 to 50 words, or turn a run of items into a bulleted list.

types.title: Words repeated by mistake
types.what: Some short words appear twice in a row, such as “the the.”
types.why: Repeated words are usually typing mistakes, and they make a page look less careful.
types.todo: Remove the extra word in each place.

types.title: YouTube videos to check for captions
types.what: These pages show videos from YouTube.
types.why: Videos need accurate captions so people who are deaf or hard of hearing can follow them. Automatic captions are often not accurate enough.
types.todo: Check that each video has accurate captions. Fix them or add them if not.

types.title: Image descriptions that don’t describe the image
types.what: Some image descriptions (alt text) start with “picture of” or “image of,” or are just a file name.
types.why: Screen readers already announce that it’s an image, and a file name tells visitors nothing about what the image shows.
types.todo: Rewrite each description to say briefly what the image shows.

types.title: Email addresses aren’t clickable
types.what: Some email addresses are plain text instead of links.
types.why: Visitors have to copy and paste the address to send an email.
types.todo: Make each address a link that starts with “mailto:”.

types.title: Placeholder text left on pages
types.what: Some pages still have “Lorem ipsum” placeholder text.
types.why: Placeholder text tells visitors the page isn’t finished.
types.todo: Replace the placeholder text with real content, or unpublish the page until it’s ready.

types.title: Lists that aren’t set up as lists
types.what: Some text looks like a list, with typed bullets or dashes, but isn’t set up as a list.
types.why: Screen readers announce a real list and how many items it has. Typed bullets are read as plain text.
types.todo: Select the items and use the bulleted or numbered list button in the editor.

types.title: Times written in a different format
types.what: A time isn’t written in the site’s standard format, such as “3:45 p.m.”
types.why: Writing times the same way everywhere makes them easier to read.
types.todo: Rewrite each time in the standard format, with a colon between the hour and minutes.

types.title: Page title is too long
types.what: This page’s title is longer than 120 characters.
types.why: Long titles are cut off in search results, and they’re tiring to hear with a screen reader.
types.todo: Shorten the title so it names the page in a few words.

types.title: Images are very large
types.what: Some images are wider than 2,000 pixels or taller than 1,000 pixels.
types.why: Oversized images make pages slow to load, especially on phones.
types.todo: Upload a smaller version of each image.

types.title: Image files are larger than 1 MB
types.what: Some image files are larger than 1 MB.
types.why: Large files make pages slow to load, especially on phones and slow connections.
types.todo: Replace each image with a smaller, compressed version.

types.title: Images that may be animated
types.what: Some GIF images are larger than 500 KB, so they may be animated.
types.why: Moving images can distract visitors and cause problems for people with some disabilities. Motion that lasts more than 5 seconds needs a way to pause it.
types.todo: Check each GIF. If it moves, replace it with a still image, or with a video visitors can pause.
